review_notes: Raw Commons GIF is visually strong for viscous fingering: an air/fluid interface invades a viscous medium and develops finger-like branches over time. Use the metadata-clean MP4 derivative for release and stable frame extraction.

New metadata-stripped derivative shows a viscous-fluid interface forming and advancing as branching finger-like air/liquid intrusions between plates. A single frame can show a branched pattern, but the named concept requires the temporal invasion and fingering sequence, so this passes as Saffman-Taylor Viscous Fingering.

The supplementary movie is a multi-panel comparison with visible PEG/SDS/particle-size labels. Although related to coffee-ring dynamics, the evidence is dominated by labeled experimental panels and final/near-final deposit patterns. Reject under the text/context-dependence and static-shortcut gates.

The movie shows lithium electrodeposition morphology along a vertical electrode, but the visible deposit does not form decisive branching dendrites, and the source title indicates a dendrite-free electrode. Reject because the target concept would depend on source metadata rather than visible dendrite growth.

Raw Commons video shows an explicit fluorescence recovery time series with red bleach/recovery ROIs and time progression, but it contains source metadata. Use the no-audio metadata-clean derivative for release; in-frame condition labels do not reveal the answer term.

New metadata-stripped derivative shows a fluorescence recovery after photobleaching time series: marked ROIs lose fluorescence after bleaching and then recover across the time sequence. A single fluorescence frame cannot identify the bleach-recovery experiment; the temporal intensity drop-and-recovery pattern supports FRAP Recovery.

The CIRA/NOAA loop shows active fire and smoke plume movement, but visible logos/timestamps remain and the wind/front-forced fire-front interpretation is too source-page dependent. Reject rather than admitting a map/satellite visualization that may not directly show a clean named fire-front propagation concept.
